title: Grammar: Future Forms — Will, Going To, Present Continuous
grammarTip:
В английском нет одного "будущего времени" — несколько форм!

WILL → спонтанное решение, предсказание, обещание:
"I'll call you later." (решил только что)
"It will rain tomorrow." (предсказание)

GOING TO → заранее запланировано / есть признаки:
"I'm going to study medicine." (уже решил)
"Look at those clouds — it's going to rain." (вижу признаки)

Present Continuous → договорённость, назначенная встреча:
"I'm meeting her at 6." (уже договорились)

Present Simple → расписание, официальные тайминги:
"The train leaves at 9:15." (официальное расписание)

💡 Совет: в 80% случаев WILL и GOING TO взаимозаменяемы!

grammarTable.subject: will + infinitive
grammarTable.short: I believe / I think / I promise
grammarTable.example: "AI will transform education." "I'll help you with that." (spontaneous offer)

grammarTable.subject: going to + infinitive
grammarTable.example: "She's going to retrain as a data analyst." "Look at those clouds — it's going to rain."

grammarTable.subject: Present continuous
grammarTable.example: "I'm meeting the team tomorrow." "They're launching the product next month."

grammarTable.subject: Present simple
grammarTable.example: "The conference starts at 9am." "The train leaves at 6."

grammarTable.subject: will be + -ing
grammarTable.verb: ongoing action at a future point
grammarTable.short: happening at that moment in future
grammarTable.example: "This time next year, I'll be working in Silicon Valley."

grammarTable.subject: will have + pp
grammarTable.example: "By 2030, renewable energy will have replaced most fossil fuels."

grammarExtra.title: Will vs Going To: Key Distinctions

rows.example: "I think electric cars will dominate by 2040." (my opinion)
"Battery costs are falling fast — EVs are going to become cheaper than petrol cars." (evidence)
"The printer is broken." "I'll fix it." (decided at the moment of speaking)
"I'm going to take a digital skills course next semester." (already decided)

grammarExtra.title: Present Continuous vs Going To for Future Plans

rows.form: Present continuous: fixed arrangement (involves other people)
rows.example: "We're presenting the report to the board on Friday." (arranged, in the diary)

rows.form: Going to: personal intention (may not be fixed)
rows.example: "I'm going to study AI ethics next year." (my intention, not yet arranged)

rows.form: Either is often acceptable for plans in spoken English
rows.example: "Are you coming to the conference?" "Yes, I'm going / I'm going to go."

grammarExtra.title: Future Time Clauses: Present Simple, NOT Will

rows.form: After time words: when, as soon as, until, by the time, once, before, after
rows.example: "When AI becomes smarter, many jobs will change." ✅

rows.form: ❌ Never use will in the time clause itself
rows.example: "When AI will become smarter, jobs will change." ❌
"If robots replace drivers, there will be massive disruption." ✅

grammarExtra.title: Future Continuous: Action in Progress at a Future Time

rows.form: will be + verb-ing = ongoing at a specific future moment
rows.example: "In 2030, millions of people will be working remotely from anywhere in the world."
"Will you be attending the tech summit?" (gentler than "Are you going?")
"I'll be passing the office anyway, so I can drop it off." (not a decision, just a natural fact)

rows.form: ❌ When AI will become advanced, jobs will change.
rows.example: ✅ When AI becomes advanced, jobs will change. (present simple in time clause)
✅ I'm going to study programming. (need "am/is/are" before "going to")

rows.form: ❌ She will meeting you at the station.
rows.example: ✅ She will meet / She's meeting you at the station.

rows.form: ❌ The future is going to being very different.
rows.example: ✅ The future is going to be very different. ("going to + bare infinitive")

exercises.text: "The printer is broken." "Don't worry — I ___ fix it."
exercises.hint: Spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking = will

exercises.text: "I've enrolled in a data science course. I ___ become a data analyst."
exercises.hint: Pre-made intention, already decided = going to

exercises.text: "We ___ (launch) the new app in March — everything is booked."

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct time clause form.
exercises.text: "When AI ___ more advanced, many jobs will change significantly."
exercises.hint: Time clauses (when/as soon as/until) use present simple, NOT will

exercises.instruction: Complete with will or going to.
exercises.text: "Look — that server is overloading. The whole system ___ crash."
exercises.hint: Visible evidence of something about to happen = going to

exercises.instruction: Which is the correct future continuous form?
exercises.text: "This time next year, she ___ her PhD in AI."
exercises.hint: Future continuous: action in progress at a specific future time

exercises.text: "As soon as the software ___ (ready), we ___ (start) testing."
exercises.hint: Time clause: present simple; result: will

exercises.instruction: Which sentence is a spontaneous offer?
opts: I'm going to help you with the project.
We're meeting the client on Wednesday.
She plans to study AI ethics.
exercises.hint: Spontaneous offer = will (decided now, not planned before)

exercises.text: "I'm not sure — I think technology ___ create as many jobs as it destroys."

exercises.instruction: Complete the future continuous polite enquiry.
exercises.text: "___ you ___ (attend) the AI ethics workshop next week?"
exercises.hint: Polite enquiry about plans: Will you be + -ing?

opts: She's going to being a software engineer.
She's going to be a software engineer.
She going to be a software engineer.
She's going be a software engineer.
exercises.correct: She's going to be a software engineer.
exercises.hint: "Going to" + bare infinitive: "going to be" (not "going to being")

exercises.instruction: Complete with the best future form.
exercises.text: "We ___ (not / release) the product until all testing is complete." (firm decision)
exercises.correct: 're not going to release / won't release
exercises.hint: Either going to or will works for firm future decisions

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses future time clause correctly?
opts: Once AI will be regulated, trust will increase.
Once AI is regulated, trust will increase.
Once AI is regulated, trust increases.
Once AI is regulated, trust is increasing.
exercises.correct: Once AI is regulated, trust will increase.
exercises.hint: Time clause (once): present simple; result: will

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct future form.
exercises.text: "I've already told my boss — I ___ (take) three weeks off in July."
exercises.hint: Fixed arrangement (told the boss, already arranged) = present continuous

exercises.text: "She'll be presenting her research at the conference in June." This describes…
opts: A spontaneous decision made just now
An action ongoing at a specific future time
An action completed before a future point
exercises.correct: An action ongoing at a specific future time
exercises.hint: Will be + -ing = future continuous (ongoing at a future moment)

questions.text: "I think AI ___ transform education within the next decade." Choose the correct form.
"The battery is at 1% — the phone ___ die." Choose the form.
questions.hint: Visible evidence of something about to happen = going to

questions.text: "When technology ___ (change) the job market, governments ___ (need) to respond."
questions.hint: Time clause: present simple; result clause: will

questions.text: "We ___ the investors at 3pm on Friday." (Already arranged, in the calendar.)
questions.hint: Fixed arrangement, involves other people = present continuous

questions.text: "This time next year, she ___ her new AI startup." (ongoing at a future moment)
questions.hint: Future continuous: action in progress at a specific future time

questions.text: "When AI will become more powerful, it will change everything." is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: Time clauses use present simple, NOT will: "when AI becomes"

questions.text: "As soon as we ___ (receive) the funding, we ___ (begin) development."
questions.hint: Time clause: present simple; result: will + infinitive

questions.text: "___ you ___ (use) the lab tomorrow?" (Polite enquiry about plans)
questions.hint: Polite future enquiry: Will you be + -ing?

questions.text: "I've decided — I ___ take a year off to learn programming." (pre-made intention)
questions.hint: Pre-made intention, decided before = going to

questions.text: "___ you look at this code for me?" (Polite spontaneous request — use will)

questions.hint: "Going to" + bare infinitive: "going to be promoted" NOT "going to being"
